title: BROKEN IN PIECES, A PLEASING AROMA

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'It must be prepared with oil on a griddle; bring it well-mixed and present the grain offering broken in pieces as an aroma pleasing to the LORD.'" - Lev 6:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Well-mixed, and broken in pieces. Then pleasing to the LORD.

The oil is not sprinkled on top; it is worked all the way through. God is not after a surface application. He wants what He gives us to permeate — to reach into the ordinary substance of who we are.

And then the breaking. We met this in chapter 2, and here it is again in the priest's own offering. Even the one who leads worship brings something broken.

That may be a comfort if you are serving God out of a life that has taken damage. Some of the most useful people in God's kingdom are those who have been through something. Paul spoke of a thorn in the flesh he begged God to remove, and God's answer was: My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness (2 Cor 12:9).

We treasure being whole and capable. God has never required either. He asks for what is well-mixed — genuine all the way through, not a performance — and He receives what is broken.

If you feel you have less to offer God than you once did, read the verse again. Broken in pieces, and pleasing to the LORD.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is God's work in me surface-level, or worked all the way through?
2. Have I assumed my brokenness makes me less useful to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, work Your grace all the way through me, not just on the surface. Take what is broken in my life and receive it as an offering. Amen.
